intro: A set-based overlap loses repetition. Multiset Jaccard compares the minimum and maximum token counts so repeated boilerplate affects similarity.
task: Compare repeated-token documents and observe how multiplicity changes similarity despite identical vocabularies.
requirements: left and right are lists or tuples of at most 10000 nonempty string tokens, with case preserved.
For each token let a and b be its two occurrence counts. Return sum(min(a,b))/sum(max(a,b)) as a float.
Define two empty documents to have similarity 1. A single empty document has similarity 0.

Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, except where a stricter bound is stated. Booleans are not numeric parameters. Leave all caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Count before comparing
hints.body: Each distinct token contributes one minimum and one maximum count.

hints.title: Handle the empty union
hints.body: Decide the both-empty result before performing division.

explanation: Multiset Jaccard retains token multiplicity, unlike ordinary set Jaccard. Repeating one token can lower similarity even when both documents have the same vocabulary.
The score is symmetric and lies in [0,1]. It ignores word order; n-gram multisets can introduce local order when that distinction matters.
